g.text: Rate Limiting: the fixed-window boundary bug, and token bucket handling the same burst
Same client burst, two algorithms -- limit is "100 requests / 60s"
counter resets to 0 at every 60s boundary
Counter for window 1 resets to 0 the instant 1:00 ticks over.
in a ~2-second span -- every single one allowed, because each
landed under the 100-limit of ITS OWN window.
The limit is real per-window, but the window edges are not a real time boundary to the client.
The bucket does not care about wall-clock window edges.
It only has 100 tokens to give out, ever, until they refill.
A burst that empties it is throttled immediately -- the next
request waits for a token, spaced ~0.6s apart at the refill rate.
Same burst, no edge case: the limit is enforced against a token count, not a wall-clock window.
